```{python}
import json
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import display
comparison = pd.read_csv('results/comparison.csv')
identity = json.loads(Path('results/run-identity.json').read_text())
display(comparison.groupby('outcome').size().rename('cases').to_frame())
display(comparison)
display(identity)
```

All declared scalar checks numerically verify Bülow, Ji and Held's Eq. (7),
DOI 10.1016/j.fluid.2019.03.010, on the explicit water/cation/anion species
basis described after Eq. (5) and in Eq. (8). The table gives every declared
composition, evaluator temperature and molar density, native relative
permittivity, independent reference, absolute error and tolerance. The water
permittivity override and original source-file identities are retained in the
run identity. Tables 2 and 3 supply the EOS coefficients; the zero interaction
parameters select the unfitted declaration. The positive fixed density only
selects an evaluator state and establishes no mechanical stability.

The zero-water endpoint is now evaluated through the same native
`State.bulk_relative_permittivity` readout after Engine #792. Its value,
independent reference, absolute error and unchanged tolerance are computed
from the retained comparison table above. This equation check supplies no
experimental dielectric validation or liquid equilibrium
result. Figures 3 and 5 still need calibrated model/symbol identity and
molecular-versus-species axis mapping. Figure 2 lacks its state/derivative
basis; Table 5 lacks the measurement population and weights. These unavailable
comparisons are outside the accepted scope.

The individual scalar cases are shown as a table without an interpolated
curve. The arithmetic tolerance tests native evaluation and mapping; it is
not experimental uncertainty. This notebook awaits independent delivered
review and has not been promoted for manuscript use.
